fr.elements: Main Building; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Road; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Retention Pond; Open Terrain; Vehicle Parking Area; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access; Retention Pond
fr.recommendations: Maintaining an unobstructed single access point and keeping the long driveway clear of parked vehicles or stored materials along its full length could significantly improve apparatus ingress and egress, particularly given the limited rear access to the property. Ensuring the driveway and approach remain passable for larger emergency vehicles may enhance operational effectiveness during time-sensitive responses. Clearly marking the access point from the street frontage could assist responding personnel in quickly identifying the entry under low-visibility conditions. The retention pond's proximity to open terrain and operational areas would support responder awareness during nighttime or limited-visibility operations near that portion of the property.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Heavy Brush; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Limited Defensible Space; Brushland Interface; Dense Shrub Cover; Fuel Continuity; Long Driveway; Vegetated Access Route; Water Feature; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing the density of brush and shrub cover in the immediate vicinity of the structure would meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce fuel continuity near the building. Brush growing adjacent to the structure should be thinned or cleared to create separation between combustible vegetation and the building envelope, which may reduce structure exposure and support suppression operations if fire approaches. Along the long driveway, managing vegetation to maintain adequate clearance on both sides would support firefighter access and improve conditions for emergency ingress and egress. Reducing connections between dense shrub patches across the property could interrupt fuel continuity and limit the opportunity for fire to spread toward improvements. The existing water feature represents a valuable on-site resource and maintaining it in operable condition could support suppression efforts. Continued vegetation management within the immediate structure perimeter, combined with ongoing attention to brush density in the broader surrounding area, would support long-term wildfire resilience for this property.
